source.title: Double Descent and Malign Overfitting in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Raphaël Urfin; Tony Bonnaire; Giulio Biroli; Marc Mézard

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes overfitting in diffusion models and contrasts it with supervised regression; it does not test random-label fitting or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study reports diffusion-model training and test losses, but those results concern denoising score matching with fixed noise realizations, not random image labels or the behaviors named in V1–V6. These adjacent findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures diffusion denoising losses and approximation of the empirical score, not fitting randomly assigned labels. Its Gaussian-data theory, regularization experiments and training dynamics do not test the behaviors specified in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. At finite m, diffusion models exhibit double descent and harmful overfitting toward the empirical score. The RFNN interpolation threshold is p ∼ nm, where p counts features and there are pd trainable parameters; the tested U-Net threshold is approximately p ∼ nmd, where p counts parameters. Optimally tuned ridge regularization in the theory and early stopping in U-Net experiments restore benefits from increased capacity.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes diffusion-model denoising score matching, using DDPM-style U-Nets and a random-features theory; it does not use random image labels or the supervised-learning recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported diffusion-model behavior varies with model size, number of fixed noise realizations m, and diffusion time t; early stopping and ridge regularization alter the generalization results.

fits_no_version.finding: For CelebA U-Nets with fixed noise realizations, denoising training loss approaches zero as capacity increases; population test loss peaks and then plateaus above its earlier minimum, while empirical test loss reaches its minimum in the overparameterized regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion denoising can interpolate fixed training pairs while approaching the empirical score and retaining elevated population loss.

record.problems: Empirical validation is limited to one dataset, a moderate number of samples, and models smaller than state-of-the-art models. The central U-Net curves are presented as figures; the text describes their trends but does not give exact plotted values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows were found. The study reports further diffusion-model and random-features results, but they concern diffusion-specific denoising, memorization, regularization, or generation and do not test V1–V6.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero classification training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence across label-corruption fractions.
The same supervised networks fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across random-label corruption fractions.
Whether weight decay, dropout and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-label patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Gaussian denoising targets also enter the noisy inputs, so they are not independent random labels. Generalization followed by diffusion memorization does not establish V6's real-label versus noisy-label learning order. The row states indicate inability to assess the listed versions, not absence of the reported diffusion effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and slowdown with label corruption.
Training and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: DDPM-style U-Net
rows.size_stated: n = 2048, m = 8; model size varies with p
rows.operation_detail: Varied parameter count and measured denoising training loss at fixed diffusion time.
rows.value: The training loss vanishes at the interpolation threshold; figure-only.
rows.note: The text describes the loss reaching zero at the interpolation threshold; the plotted numeric value is not transcribed.
rows.check: The reported near-zero denoising training loss is supported by Section 2.3, but cannot establish random-label or unstructured-input fitting as specified in the claim.

rows.subject: DDPM-style U-Net
rows.size_stated: n = 2048, m = 8; model size varies with p
rows.operation_detail: Varied parameter count and measured population test loss at fixed diffusion time.
rows.value: The loss first decreases, then rises to a peak and settles at a value larger than its first minimum; figure-only.
rows.note: The text describes the curve; precise plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The described population denoising-loss curve is supported by Section 2.3. It does not measure classification test error or vary the fraction of corrupted labels.

rows.subject: DDPM-style U-Net
rows.size_stated: n = 2048, m = 8; model size varies with p
rows.operation_detail: Varied parameter count and measured empirical test loss at fixed diffusion time.
rows.value: Tracks the training loss and reaches its minimum in the overparameterized regime; figure-only.
rows.note: The empirical test loss measures distance to the empirical score, not random-label test error.
rows.check: The described curve is supported by Section 2.3. Empirical test loss evaluates fresh noises around training images and measures approximation of the empirical score; it cannot establish any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
